## 4. THE HOLE, which is the one thing a close may name and may not fill

**`chapters/volume-10/chapter-0475.md` DOES NOT EXIST.** Day 475, a Sunday, the hundred and sixtieth day of the Bare Month, the volume's nearer of its two middle days — a fifty-day range has two, 475 and 476, and neither may be called the midpoint. **`outline/volume-10.md` §8 is the chapter: a decision taken out loud, in daylight, with a date in chalk on the door, about nine people present, by a woman of about twenty-nine who keeps a public register, after she has named the cost out loud first, and the cost is hers. It is that this city's own figure goes on the store's board in chalk beside the figures of the two hundred and twenty-fourth day and that the two sets stay side by side and neither is rubbed out, and that a surface which has stood unwritten since the two hundred and twenty-fifth day of this flood stops being able to be silent the moment it says something, and cannot be given back, and the man who has been keeping it silent is not the person who pays. Adrian Vale is not in it and §8 says so in its own words and a card may not put him in it.** The batch behind the one behind this one wrote nine chapters across days 471 to 480 with no gap and was told that Chapter 0475 is not its, and it did not write it. **Chapters 0476, 0477, 0478, 0479 and 0480 refer to what was said in that room on that Sunday, and Chapter 0490 puts on a wall the figure that decision was about, and a reader of Chapter 0500 has been given the fact of a decision without ever being given the scene. A HUNDRED AND TWENTY-FIVE CHAPTER FILES CARRY A REFERENCE TO A ROOM THAT NO PAGE IN THIS REPOSITORY SUPPLIES.**

**A CLOSE IS THE ONE PHASE IN THIS REPOSITORY THAT IS ALLOWED TO NAME A CHAPTER THAT IS NOT THERE, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE OF WHAT IT IS ALLOWED TO DO WITH THIS ONE.** Your close record must name the hole, give the day, the weekday, the Bare-Month ordinal, the section of the plan that is the chapter, and the cost of leaving it, and it must say who the hole belongs to. **It may not write the chapter. It may not summarise what was decided as though it had been read. It may not decide anything in it. IT MAY NOT ROUTE THE CHAPTER TO A BATCH, because filling it is deciding something and a batch decides nothing, and it may not route it to a repair pass, because a repair pass that quietly takes a routed item to save itself a line is the failure `state/volume-09-close.md` §7.7 names and has now cost this repository four times.** **IF YOU TAKE ANYTHING FROM THIS CLOSE, TAKE THIS: the debt for Chapter 0475 is owed to the next OUTLINE phase or to a Volume 11 close, and the debt for the four missing card files at `outline/batches/volume-10-batch-0002.md`, `-0003.md`, `-0004.md` and `-0005.md` is owed to the next OUTLINE phase, and NEITHER IS OWED BY A WRITER AND NEITHER IS OWED BY A REPAIR PASS, and a close may record both and may pay neither.** And if a Volume 11 outline phase writes the card files, it must be told that a card file written after the chapters are on disk is a reconstruction, which is why the five batches that had none each wrote its cards at the head of its own state record before its first chapter, and that is the arrangement `outline/volume-10.md` §21 made and the next outline inherits and does not reopen.

## 6. The next phase, by path, and it is an OUTLINE

**`workspace/volume-11/outline/PROMPT.md`, and it is a VOLUME OUTLINE PHASE and not a batch and not a close.** It writes `outline/volume-11.md`, Volume 11's first batch's cards at `outline/batches/volume-11-batch-0001.md`, its own block in `outline/series.md`, and the four state files repointed at its own path, and no prose. **It is the only kind of phase after a close that is allowed to decide, and this close leaves it the nine decisions of record this volume inherited, the four this close has added, the four debts it has named, and the six open questions below.**

**AND THE SIX QUESTIONS A VOLUME 11 OUTLINE PHASE OWES AN ANSWER TO, WHICH ARE THE SIX THINGS THIS VOLUME LEFT OPEN ON PURPOSE, AND NONE OF THEM IS A MYSTERY AND NONE OF THEM IS A HUNT.** What is a word for, in a count, when the only thing anybody will use it for is to make two numbers the same — asked once, on day 498, to one man, and not answered, and the room did not hear it, and a later volume may ask it again in a mouth in a room in daylight with a date on the door and may not answer it. The one of four marks that came back out of place on the sheet of day 440, which is not traced and is not going to be traced by a reader of this volume, and a later volume may not trace it unless tracing it is a decision to trace it. The fence, and whether it stands between the right two things, which is not settled and which no chapter of fifty measured. The man of about fifty-seven, and the length of new rope he has never used, and the fact that nobody in this city asked him about either. The three on a four-hundred-mile road, a hundred and nine days out at day 500, measured from day 391, and not one person on that road can be shown to anybody in this city. And the seventh form of the calendar, which does not exist and which comes onto a page the moment the end of the Bare Month is on one, by a person, in a room, in daylight, with a date on the door.
